blocks.text: Mastering Chrome for literary agents on Mac

Most agents spend their day in a browser. You track submissions, check deal sites, and manage emails in Gmail. Chrome is the industry standard, but it can feel cluttered. Keeping your tabs organized is the first step to sanity. Use ⌘ + 1 through ⌘ + 8 to jump between open tabs. This stops you from clicking around aimlessly. If you have too many tabs, use ⌘ + ⇧ + A to search for the one you need.
Using voice to speed up your research

When you are researching a new author or market trends, you often open dozens of tabs. This slows down your Mac. Instead, ask Lazur to perform research. It opens its own background tabs to gather information. It then gives you a summary. You stay focused on the current task. Hold ⌥ ⌘ to ask about a specific site. Lazur can explain complex pages or point to specific data points.
Keyboard shortcuts for daily agency tasks

items: ⌘ + T: Open a new tab for a quick search.
⌘ + L: Highlight the address bar to enter a URL.
⌘ + ⇧ + T: Reopen the last tab you closed by accident.
⌘ + ⌥ + Right Arrow: Switch to the next tab quickly.
⌘ + W: Close the current tab after you finish a task.

blocks.text: If you find yourself opening the same sites every morning, add them to your Bookmarks Bar. Press ⌘ + ⇧ + B to toggle the bar on or off. Keep it clean so you do not get distracted.
blocks.title: Clean up your workspace

blocks.text: Pitching requires a personal touch. Typing the same phrases over and over takes time. Use the fn key to dictate your thoughts directly into Gmail or your editor. Lazur formats the text as you speak. You can dictate a quick response to an author or a draft for a publisher. This keeps your hands on the keyboard for editing instead of typing from scratch.

You handle sensitive contract information and private author details. You need tools that respect that. Lazur does not store your screen or audio. It processes everything on your Mac. Nothing is sent to train models. This is vital when you are reviewing confidential manuscripts in your browser.

items: Keeping too many extensions active: This slows down your browser and causes crashes.
Ignoring browser updates: Update your Chrome to keep security patches current.
Not using profiles: Create separate profiles for personal and agency work to keep your history clean.
Saving passwords in the browser without a master lock: Use a dedicated manager for sensitive data.

blocks.text: How to get help with Lazur

If you are stuck, ask Lazur to guide you. Say 'How do I clear my cache?' and Lazur will walk you through the Menu > Settings > Privacy and Security path. It waits for you to click each step. It does not take control, so you always know exactly what is happening on your Mac.

faq.question: Does Lazur work inside Gmail?
faq.answer: Yes. You can use the fn key to dictate emails or ask Lazur to summarize long threads while you are in your Gmail tab.

faq.question: Can Lazur read my private contracts?
faq.answer: Lazur only sees your screen when you hold the shortcut. It does not store your data. Your privacy is protected.

faq.question: Is Lazur an extension for Chrome?
faq.answer: Lazur is a Mac app that lives in your notch. It works across every app, including Chrome, without needing to be installed as an extension.
